items: The revised forecast must account ____ recent changes in fuel prices and shipping fees.
The verb 'account' takes the preposition 'for' when explaining or allowing for something.
The hotel manager apologized ____ the delay in preparing the conference rooms.
The verb 'apologize' takes the preposition 'for' before the reason for an apology.
The purchasing director insisted ____ reviewing all bids before a supplier was selected.
The verb 'insist' takes the preposition 'on' before a noun or gerund.
The regional market has recovered ____ last year's temporary decline in consumer spending.
A prolonged equipment failure could result ____ significant production delays.
The expression 'result in' means to cause a particular outcome.
Our premium service differs ____ the standard plan in both response time and coverage.
The verb 'differ' commonly takes the preposition 'from' when contrasting two things.
All laptops issued by the company belong ____ the information technology department.
Ms. Ortega will deal ____ customer complaints while the service manager is away.
The phrasal verb 'deal with' means to handle or address something.
The manufacturer plans to invest ____ more energy-efficient production equipment next year.
Department heads should prepare ____ the annual budget meeting by reviewing current expenses.
The verb 'prepare' takes the preposition 'for' before an event or situation.
Several applicants inquired ____ the possibility of working remotely two days per week.
The verb 'inquire' can take 'about' when asking for information concerning a topic.
The auditor declined to comment ____ the findings until the final report was released.
The verb 'comment' takes the preposition 'on' when referring to a topic.
New scheduling software will allow the support team to adapt ____ changes in call volume more quickly.
The verb 'adapt' takes the preposition 'to' when adjusting to a condition or change.
The finance team relies ____ weekly sales reports when updating its cash-flow projections.
Employees who work at least twenty hours per week may qualify ____ subsidized transportation passes.
The verb 'qualify' takes the preposition 'for' before a benefit or opportunity.
The consulting team will engage ____ a detailed review of the client's inventory procedures.
The verb 'engage' takes the preposition 'in' before an activity.
The protective packaging helps prevent delicate components ____ being damaged during transit.
The verb 'prevent' takes 'from' before a gerund in the pattern 'prevent something from doing/being done'.
The project manager will negotiate ____ the contractor about the revised completion date.
The verb 'negotiate' takes 'with' for the person or organization involved in negotiations.
The delivery company does not charge customers ____ standard weekend service.
The verb 'charge' takes the preposition 'for' before the service or item being billed.
Several investors are concerned ____ the effect of rising material costs on quarterly earnings.
The adjective 'concerned' takes 'about' when expressing worry regarding something.
Most participants said they were satisfied ____ the practical exercises included in the workshop.
The adjective 'satisfied' commonly takes the preposition 'with'.
The coastal region is known ____ its highly skilled shipbuilding workforce.
The expression 'be known for' identifies a notable quality or feature.
Two senior engineers are involved ____ the testing of the new battery-management system.
The adjective/participle 'involved' takes 'in' before an activity or project.
The neighborhood association remains opposed ____ the proposed expansion of the distribution center.
The company is committed ____ reducing packaging waste by 30 percent over the next three years.
The expression 'be committed to' takes 'to', followed here by a gerund.
